A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HoliTom, with matching methods, main experiments, and identifiable appendix material. The text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison across both complete documents.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, inference measurements, ablations, and qualitative examples, including Tables 2–5 and Figures 3–11.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds Qwen2.5-VL evaluations, object-subtask results, efficiency measurements, and a merging-strategy comparison in Tables 6–9.

M1.justification: The temporal segmentation, attention-guided spatial selection, DPC-KNN clustering, and inner-LLM merging procedures remain unchanged. The Qwen2.5-VL experiment uses the existing outer-only variant with different settings; it does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four video-understanding benchmarks. The added Qwen2.5-VL evaluation uses VideoMME, while the object analysis reports existing MVBench subtasks. Changes to backbones, frame sampling, and resolution handling concern experimental settings rather than new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds separately evaluated Attention and DPC-KNN alternatives against HoliTom's mixed merging strategy. The six named external baselines and their original comparisons remain unchanged. Table 6 reuses FastV, VisionZip, and PruneVid; FastV is reported as running out of memory.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a substantially different Qwen2.5-VL-7B evaluation: 2-fps sampling, up to 768 frames, dynamic-resolution support, a 24,576-token cap, and temporal threshold 0.2. Only outer-LLM compression is evaluated successfully because inner-LLM attention encounters memory limits. Existing LLaVA protocols are retained; these are added settings, not documented revisions or reruns of the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether compression preserves object existence, interaction, and shuffle performance (Table 7), and whether mixed merging outperforms attention-only or clustering-only strategies (Table 9). Table 8 also adds computational costs to the existing frame-scaling analysis. The earlier threshold ablation and qualitative examples are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additions continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and Figures 1–11 retain their results, but Tables 6–9 substantially expand the reported evidence. Table 6 adds Qwen2.5-VL outer-only scores of 65.8 at 102.0 TFLOPs and 64.8 at 66.9 TFLOPs; Table 9 reports averages of 58.5 for mixed merging, 58.1 for Attention, and 56.9 for DPC-KNN. Object-subtask scores are newly reported. Table 8 repeats Figure 4's accuracy values while adding FLOP costs for larger frame counts.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, including the segmentation objective, dynamic-programming recurrence, clustering definitions, merging rule, and FLOP calculation, are unchanged. The added appendix discussion introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims, including 99.1% performance at 6.9% FLOPs, 2.28× TTFT acceleration, and 1.32× decoding throughput. The appendix additions provide supporting evidence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets object-subtask results as evidence of fine-grained information preservation and identifies memory limits preventing Qwen2.5-VL inner-LLM evaluation. It also discusses increasing vision-encoder overhead with more frames. The original streaming and vision-tower limitations remain, and the mixed-merging rationale largely restates Section 3.3.

D1.justification: Appendix A and Table 6 provide settings for the added Qwen2.5-VL experiment, including threshold 0.2, sampling rate, frame cap, token cap, and the definition of reported token counts. Existing hardware, LLaVA configurations, baseline settings, evaluation framework, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds nine references, including VideoChat-Flash, Video-XL, QUOTA, StreamVLN, and SpecPrune-VLA, through expanded background citations and future-work suggestions. The substantive related-work narrative and positioning of HoliTom relative to existing compression methods remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main text receives limited wording corrections, updated affiliations and conference identification, and an acknowledgment. Appendix B becomes Supplemental Experimental Results with five subsections; its original threshold discussion moves to B.4. There is no extensive rewriting of the main narrative.

P2.justification: Four appendix tables are added, including the side-by-side Tables 7–8. Existing Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–11 retain their substantive displays, while appendix figures and subsequent sections are repositioned. The presentation changes are localized additions and reflow rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1's LLaVA evaluations, Table 6 provides useful evidence on another model family, and Table 9 directly tests the previously motivated mixed-merging choice. The added subtask and computational-cost results improve empirical scrutiny. These gains are limited: Qwen2.5-VL validates only outer merging, and Table 7's mixed, nonmonotonic scores do not fully support its broad improvement wording. Overall, the added evidence modestly strengthens the paper.
